text:
Maya (CEO): Morning team — quick field snapshot before the week. High-level asks: stabilize EU private beta, hit cost target v0.9 (-12% unit cost by next quarter), and finalize two rollback/runbook items. Please scan the bullets and flag blockers. :wave:

Liam (VP Eng): Got it. Eng will prioritize a hotfix for session caching to cut tail latency. ETA by end of week. I'll assign PR reviews and call out any infra deps.

Jon (Head of SRE): We'll run a canary tomorrow 09:00 PST. Plan: canary->regional rollout with strict traffic caps. Alerts to watch: 429s, increased p95 decode time, KV-cache evictions. I'll add an automated fallback policy.

Priya (VP Product): Drafted customer comms for early access — will share shortly. Request: freeze non-critical feature merges Wed-Fri next week to minimize churn during beta.

Sam (Finance): Cost approach: batching + aggressive quant profiles for background workloads. I'm updating the forecast; preliminary modeling shows ~11% savings if we hit utilization targets. I'll post the spreadsheet.

Amanda (Security): Heads-up: EU private beta requires updated DLP checklist and key rotation confirmation. I added the two missing items to the Compliance board and pinged infra for KMS verification.

Emily (Customer Success): We'll prep outreach for the top 5 early adopters and schedule onboarding sessions. Sharing briefing slides to the thread in a bit.

OpsBot: Deployment pipeline queued: build 2026.04.03.canary.7. Notifying subscribers in #release-war-room.

Maya (CEO): Thanks — concrete asks from me: 1) No non-essential merges during the canary window. 2) SRE to post rollback runbook (one-click) and acceptance criteria in this thread. 3) PMs to confirm comms cadence for customers and legal/compliance sign-off.

Liam (VP Eng): Acknowledged. We'll mute non-critical alerts during the canary, and post the rollback script as `scripts/rollback_canary.sh` in the repo. Will also add a short README for on-call.

Jon (Head of SRE): Rollback runbook uploaded to Confluence and summarized here: 1) halt frontend routing -> 2) switch traffic to fallback model variant -> 3) invalidate KV cache -> 4) restore previous model version. I added a one-liner to trigger it. Canary scheduled: 2026-04-03 16:00 UTC. :white_check_mark:

Priya (VP Product): Shared the comms draft: https://docs.redwood.ai/internal/comms/eu-private-beta-draft — please comment by EOD. Requesting sign-off from Legal and Security before we hit public beta.

Emily (Customer Success): Slide pack uploaded and brief invites sent for Monday sync with the first cohort. Will surface any usability flags.

Maya (CEO): Quick risk notes: monitor latency regressions closely (p95), watch early-usage cost trends, and escalate any customer-impacting errors immediately. Small wins: keep the team focused on those three metrics — availability, unit cost, and customer onboarding NPS.

Liam (VP Eng): We'll add a hold on non-urgent infra changes and post rollout notes to #release-war-room once canary begins.

Jon (Head of SRE): Pinged the oncall rotation and will post real-time status updates during the run.

OpsBot: Canary execution started by @lifecyclebot. Live logs: https://logs.redwood.ai/build/2026.04.03.canary.7

Maya (CEO): Appreciated. Short check-in Monday AM to confirm metrics and next steps. Enjoy the weekend and recharge. :slightly_smiling_face:
